rationale: The literature universally confirms that congenital contractures and arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (HP:0002804), including distal joint contractures of the hands and feet, are defining cardinal manifestations of FILIP1-related neuromuscular disorder. However, the proposed frequency estimate of 60–80% is contradicted by the reported literature: across published cohorts (e.g., Schnabel et al. 2023, Watts et al. 2024, Chaurasia et al. 2026), congenital multiple joint contractures are documented in 100% (e.g., 5/5 in Schnabel et al.) of affected individuals rather than only 60–80%.

evidence.text: Five affected individuals from three independent families sharing homozygous truncating variants in FILIP1 presented with an overlapping phenotype with congenital contractures affecting shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee, and foot (5/5, 100%), alongside scoliosis, reduced palmar/plantar skin folds, microcephaly, and dysmorphic features.

source.title: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 cause autosomal recessive arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with microcephaly
source.quote: Here, we report five affected individuals from three independent families sharing an overlapping phenotype with congenital contractures affecting shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee and foot as well as scoliosis, reduced palmar and plantar skin folds, microcephaly and facial dysmorphism.

conflicts: The hypothesis posits a 60–80% penetrance for congenital contractures/arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, whereas empirical cohort data demonstrate that 100% (e.g., 5/5 in Schnabel et al. 2023) of described individuals have congenital joint contractures, making 60–80% an underestimate based on currently published case series.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true frequency of contractures when FILIP1 is screened unbiasedly across general neurodevelopmental cohorts rather than ascertainment-biased arthrogryposis cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Current literature primarily identifies FILIP1 variants via targeted cohorts recruited specifically for arthrogryposis multiplex congenita or congenital joint contractures, which artificially inflates contracture penetrance toward 100%.

new_directions.question_text: Which distinct dysmorphic facial features reliably discriminate FILIP1-related congenital myopathy from other genetic causes of arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (e.g., MET, KLHL40, LAMA2)?
new_directions.rationale: Because congenital contractures are shared across many arthrogryposis syndromes, detailed phenotypic cataloging of facial features, palmar/plantar crease abnormalities, and CNS/cranial MRI findings is critical for differential diagnosis prior to genomic confirmation.
